settings.introHTML: This lesson teaches you how to make arrangements in French, whether you are phoning someone, suggesting an outing, or agreeing a time to meet. You will practise useful expressions such as Tu veux aller... ?, Je veux bien, À quelle heure ?, and C'est dommage ! while learning how to accept, refuse, and reorganise plans politely.
settings.informationHTML:
After completing this unit, you will be able to:

  • Ask for and give contact details before arranging to meet.
  • Invite someone to places such as the cinema, swimming pool, café, or shopping centre.
  • Use vouloir to express what someone wants or does not want to do.
  • Use à, au, à la, à l', and aux more accurately with places.
  • Recognise and pronounce common French words with the ui sound.

dialogues.informationTextHTML: This section introduces short conversations for exchanging phone numbers, checking information, and arranging to meet up.

phraseTable1.informationTextHTML: Read each line, then play the audio to hear how the telephone number is spoken.
phrases: Quel est ton numéro de portable ?
Quel est votre numéro de téléphone s'il vous plaît Madame ?
What's your phone number please, Madam?

phraseTable2.informationTextHTML: Listen for the language used to check a number, apologise, and end the call politely when there has been a mistake.
phrases: Ah non, je suis désolée, il y a une erreur ! C'est le 01 23 08 08 16.
Oh no, I'm sorry, there's a mistake. This is 01 23 08 08 16.

phraseTable3.informationTextHTML: Notice how the conversation moves from the phone call itself to making plans for later.
phrases: André est là, s'il vous plaît ?
André, tu veux prendre un verre avec moi ce soir ?
André, do you want to have a drink with me this evening?
Oui, je veux bien. À quelle heure ?
Yes, I'd like that. At what time?

phraseTable4.informationTextHTML: Focus on the invitation, the agreed time, and the short expressions speakers use to confirm their plans.
phrases: Tu veux aller au cinéma demain ?
Do you want to go to the cinema tomorrow?
Oui, je veux bien ! À quelle heure ?
Yes, I'd like to do that! At what time?
At 3 o' clock? Is that alright?
Ah oui, ça va très bien !
phraseTable4.titleText: Arranging to go to the cinema

vocabulary.informationTextHTML: This section introduces the key verbs, time expressions, places, and social phrases used when making arrangements.

You will learn:

  • Useful invitation and response phrases such as Je veux bien, Pas de problème, and C'est dommage.
  • Days of the week and common time expressions for arranging to meet.
  • Place vocabulary such as cinéma, piscine, restaurant, and centre commercial.
  • A wider bank of activity verbs that can be used after vouloir.
phrases: Tu veux aller… ? Vous voulez aller… ?

I'd like to.
(Set expression used to accept an invitation.)
lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday
à une heure, à deux heures, à trois heures, à quatre heures …
At 1 o'clock, at 2 o'clock, at 3 o'clock, at 4 o'clock…

holiday(s)
(Always used in the plural in French)

instructionsLayout.paragraphHTML: This section explains how vouloir is used to make plans and how à changes before different place nouns.

grammar1.informationTextHTML: In this part, focus on how vouloir changes with the subject and how it is followed by an infinitive when you say what someone wants to do.

grammar2.menuText: 2. au / à la / à l' / aux
grammar2.informationTextHTML: Here, concentrate on the different forms of à before masculine, feminine, vowel, and plural nouns so you can say where you are going more naturally.

pronunciation1.informationTextHTML: In this part, focus on how the letters ui sound in common French words. Listen carefully and repeat each example aloud.

pronunciation2.informationTextHTML: Extend the same pronunciation pattern to a few more familiar words, then compare them with the examples in the first tab.

selectExercise1.informationTextHTML: Listen to the poem Chacun à son goût ! and choose the correct form of vouloir for each line. Work through the whole poem first, then use Check answers to review your choices, Show answers for support, and Reset to try again.

Tu [*veux|veut|voulons|voulez|veulent] dormir.
Annie [veux|*veut|voulons|voulez|veulent] courir.
Dani [veux|*veut|voulons|voulez|veulent] tricoter.
Lucie [veux|*veut|voulons|voulez|veulent] papoter.
Millie [veux|*veut|voulons|voulez|veulent] méditer.
Nous [veux|veut|*voulons|voulez|veulent] bouquiner.
Vous [veux|veut|voulons|*voulez|veulent] bavarder.
Mes amis [veux|veut|voulons|voulez|*veulent] dessiner.
Les enfants [veux|veut|voulons|voulez|*veulent] grandir.

selectExercise2.informationTextHTML: Play each French sentence and choose the matching English meaning. Work through all the items first, then use Check answers to review your choices, Show answers for support, and Reset to try again.

items.text: Martin veut acheter un vélo. [*Martin wants to buy a bike.|My friends want to visit the old town.|We want to play badminton tomorrow evening.|I want to go to the cinema on Friday.|Angèle wants to have a drink with her friends.|I don't want to sing in the choir.]

Mes amis veulent visiter la vieille ville. [*My friends want to visit the old town.|Martin wants to buy a bike.|Do you want to make an appointment for tomorrow?|We want to play badminton tomorrow evening.|Do you want to live in the town centre?|Angèle wants to have a drink with her friends.]

Vous voulez prendre un rendez-vous pour demain ? [*Do you want to make an appointment for tomorrow?|Do they want to do some shopping tomorrow morning?|Do you want to live in the town centre?|Martin wants to buy a bike.|We want to play badminton tomorrow evening.|I don't want to sing in the choir.]

Nous voulons jouer au badminton demain soir. [*We want to play badminton tomorrow evening.|My friends want to visit the old town.|Do you want to make an appointment for tomorrow?|I want to go to the cinema on Friday.|They don't want to play football today.|Angèle wants to have a drink with her friends.]

Ils veulent faire du shopping demain matin ? [*Do they want to do some shopping tomorrow morning?|Do you want to make an appointment for tomorrow?|Do you want to live in the town centre?|My friends want to visit the old town.|I want to go to the cinema on Friday.|Angèle wants to have a drink with her friends.]

Je veux aller au cinéma vendredi. [*I want to go to the cinema on Friday.|Martin wants to buy a bike.|Do you want to live in the town centre?|Do they want to do some shopping tomorrow morning?|Angèle wants to have a drink with her friends.|I don't want to sing in the choir.]

Tu veux habiter au centre-ville ? [*Do you want to live in the town centre?|Do you want to make an appointment for tomorrow?|Do they want to do some shopping tomorrow morning?|Martin wants to buy a bike.|My friends want to visit the old town.|I don't want to sing in the choir.]

Elles ne veulent pas jouer au foot aujourd'hui. [*They don't want to play football today.|We want to play badminton tomorrow evening.|Do they want to do some shopping tomorrow morning?|Martin wants to buy a bike.|Do you want to live in the town centre?|I don't want to sing in the choir.]

Angèle veut prendre un verre avec ses amis. [*Angèle wants to have a drink with her friends.|Martin wants to buy a bike.|My friends want to visit the old town.|I want to go to the cinema on Friday.|We want to play badminton tomorrow evening.|Do they want to do some shopping tomorrow morning?]

Je ne veux pas chanter dans la chorale. [*I don't want to sing in the choir.|They don't want to play football today.|Do you want to make an appointment for tomorrow?|I want to go to the cinema on Friday.|Do you want to live in the town centre?|Angèle wants to have a drink with her friends.]

inlineChoiceGroup3.informationTextHTML: Choose au, à la, à l', or aux to complete each sentence correctly. Then use Check answers to review your choices.

items.text: Je vais [au|*à la|à l'|aux] bibliothèque.
Ma copine travaille [au|*à la|à l'|aux] pharmacie.
Je vais [*au|à la|à l'|aux] centre commercial.
Nous allons [au|*à la|à l'|aux] piscine.
Les enfants sont [au|à la|*à l'|aux] école.
Mon bureau se trouve [*au|à la|à l'|aux] centre-ville.
Vous allez [au|à la|*à l'|aux] exposition ?
Le professeur écrit une lettre [au|à la|à l'|*aux] étudiants.
Tu veux dîner [*au|à la|à l'|aux] restaurant ce soir ?
J'aime passer mes vacances [au|à la|à l'|*aux] Pays-Bas.

dictationExercise4.informationTextHTML: Listen to each line of the dialogue and type exactly what you hear. Use the whole conversation to help you predict the missing words and expressions.
phrases: [Patrick, tu veux jouer au tennis aujourd'hui ?]
[Je ne sais pas. À quelle heure ?]
[Ah non, à 2 heures ça ne va pas ! Ce n'est pas possible !]
[Oh c'est dommage ! Pourquoi ? Tu as cours aujourd'hui ?]
[Non, je n'ai pas de cours aujourd'hui, mais j'ai un rendez-vous avec mon prof à 2 heures.]
[Ah oui, je veux bien. Je suis libre à partir de 4 heures !]

instructionsLayout.paragraphHTML: This section gives you a chance to practise the key points from this unit. You will check your forms of vouloir for what people want to do, choose the correct contraction of à when naming places, and complete short listening and dictation tasks set in everyday plans.
